Elena / team —

A few technical clarifications to make the auditor's job easier (and to avoid unnecessary exports):

1) HSM attestation: the vendor-signed PDF includes firmware versions, HSM serial ranges, and FIPS/CC statement. We keep attestation snapshots per-cluster. The PDF attached is the December 2026 snapshot — if you need the June 2026 snapshot for comparison let us know.

2) Rotation-runbook trace: the runbook is invoked by our orchestration service; each invocation produces a signed record with:
   - invocation_id (e.g., inv-2026-11-03-7c9b)
   - triggered_by (service account id)
   - prior_kek_digest and new_kek_digest (sha256)
   - wrap/unwrap trace entries for tenant BYOK flows

   We exported the runbook traces into rotation_logs_2025-01-01_to_2026-12-31.zip. Note that the tenant-specific wrapped-key blobs are redacted; the runbook trace contains digests and timestamps which are sufficient for auditors to validate rotation frequency and continuity without revealing plaintext or tenant keys.

3) KMS operator access matrix: we will provide the role->subject mapping CSV. For audit purposes we can also provide IAM policy snapshots for the past two rotations. PII fields (operator emails, external IPs) will be redacted unless the auditor submits an NDA.

4) In-transit wrapping: our transit path always performs an envelope wrap at TLS termination and then immediately re-wraps with tenant KEK for BYOK enabled customers. We can provide packet-level cipher suites inventory (from our TLS telemetry) as a CSV if needed.

If Bridgecrest's auditor needs a short statement of methodology from our crypto team (1 page) summarizing how we guarantee non-repudiable rotation records, I can draft that and include it in the index.

-Jonas
